source_documents.title: Rigid Boron‐Fused Frameworks for Efficient Near‐Infrared Emission and Optical Gain Beyond 900 nm

reference_evidence_units.quote: The resulting emitters exhibited reduced knr s, enhanced photoluminescence quantum yields, and higher external electroluminescence quantum efficiencies in NIR organic light-emitting diodes relative to a conventional donor-based analogue.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BBT-DABNA, BBT-OABNA vs BBT-TPA
reference_evidence_units.statement: Boron-fused MR units lower knr and raise PLQY relative to the triphenylamine analogue.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Analysis of the rate constants revealed that these improvements originated not only from enhanced kr but also from suppressed knr (Table 1).
reference_evidence_units.subject: BBT-MR compounds
reference_evidence_units.statement: Both larger kr and smaller knr.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The PLQYs of the spin-coated films were 7.2%, 7.7%, and 14.5% for BBT-TPA, BBT-DABNA, and BBTOABNA, respectively
reference_evidence_units.subject: all three

reference_evidence_units.quote: Despite possessing similarly fused and structurally constrained skeletons, the MR compounds exhibited smaller structural displacements and suppressed strongly coupled vibrational modes, indicating more delocalized structural relaxation and weaker electronvibrational coupling.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BBT-MR compounds
reference_evidence_units.statement: Smaller Huang-Rhys factors and reorganization energies for the MR compounds.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Notably, BBT-OABNA exhibited approximately a twofold increase in PLQY compared to BBT-TPA, owing to the effective suppression of knr , demonstrating the effectiveness of the rigid boron-framework design strategy for developing high-performance NIR-emitting materials.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BBT-OABNA vs BBT-TPA

reference_evidence_units.quote: MR-derived boron-fused frameworks were incorporated to suppress electron– vibration coupling while maintaining long-wavelength emission arising from long-range CT excited states.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BBT-MR compounds
reference_evidence_units.statement: The emission comes from long-range CT states.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Emission arises from long-range CT excited states (conclusion); the CT character is shared and does not explain the differences.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Energy-gap-law framing: knr is the bottleneck in the NIR, and the paper explains the PLQY order by knr (and kr) from Table 1 plus Huang-Rhys analysis. BBT-OABNA has the smallest knr and twice the PLQY of BBT-TPA.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Rigid frameworks act through weaker vibronic coupling in the energy-gap law (guideline §3.5 first bullet, awaiting the author); not labelled RIM.

contrast_group.paper_difference: The rigid boron-fused donors weaken electron-vibration coupling, lower knr and raise PLQY (7.2% to 14.5% in film) at >860 nm.
